title: Creating a browsing context incorrectly assumes a hierarchy when initializing its document.
body:
Originally opened as w3c/webappsec-feature-policy#284:

> > When HTML creates a browsing context it calls this algorithm, but this expects the document to already participate in some hierarchy that hasn't yet been established. Either creator needs to be passed in or this needs to work entirely differently.
>
> To be clear, is this a result of the document's browsing context being a nested browsing context with no browsing context container yet?
>
> (I was looking at the Implement the sandboxing algorithm, which is called from the same place, and it seems to also assume the parent-child browsing context relationship, so I'm trying to disentangle the exact differences to see how to best fix this)

@annevk as original opener

It looks like the "[Create a new browsing context](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsers.html#creating-a-new-browsing-context)" steps should be changed to allow sandboxing and feature policy to be initialized *after* the browsing context is part of the hierarchy. That is, after the auxiliary / nested browsing context specific steps have been run.

The easiest way to do this in the spec is probably to move steps 12 and 13, and probably 14, into each of [create a new auxiliary browsing context](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsers.html#creating-a-new-auxiliary-browsing-context), [create a new nested browsing context](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsers.html#creating-a-new-nested-browsing-context), and [create a new browsing context group](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsers.html#creating-a-new-browsing-context-group).

(If it's okay to move step 14 before initializing sandbox and feature policy, then it can remain in the original algorithm)
